title: Filing against in-laws - is it legally sustainable
p1:
Can a case against in-laws survive in court, or is it automatically dismissed?

Many people assume that once a matrimonial dispute begins, every family member of the spouse can be named. But the law does not work that way.
p2: A lesser-known point is that courts often look beyond relationships and examine specific allegations. Being an in-law alone does not create legal liability. There must be clear facts showing involvement in the alleged wrongdoing.
p3:
For example, vague statements that family members harassed someone may not be enough. Courts generally expect details about what happened, when it happened, and how the person was involved.

The practical lesson: filing against in-laws can be legally sustainable, but only when supported by specific allegations and evidence. A complaint based only on family connections may face serious challenges.
